You are analyzing the "memos" codebase at /bench/repo (Go backend). Search breadth: very thorough. Answer with exact path:line citations.

Q1 (h10): Which single function or method declared under internal/ (the internal/ directory of this repo, e.g. internal/util, internal/base, internal/profile) has the highest inbound-call count (fan-in) across the repo? Approach: list exported functions in internal/* packages, grep for their usages (e.g. util.GenUUID, base.ConvertToPascalCase, etc.), count call sites, and report the winner: symbol — declaration path:line — approximate number of callers. Mention the runner-up too.

Q2 (h11): Of the persistent entity/model types defined in the data layer (the store package: e.g. store.Memo, store.User, store.Attachment/Resource, store.Activity, store.Workspace...), which one is referenced from the largest number of packages OUTSIDE the store layer? Count distinct packages (directories) outside store/ that reference each type (grep for "store.User", "store.Memo", etc.). Rank the top two with rough package counts.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
## Q1 — Highest fan-in function/method under `internal/`

**Winner: `util.GenUUID` — `/bench/repo/internal/util/util.go:40` — 28 call sites, all of them outside the declaring package.**

It is the only `internal/` symbol whose callers are *entirely* external, and it has the largest cross-package call count by a wide margin.

Call sites (28 total, 8 distinct files, 4 distinct packages):
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/auth_test.go` — 19
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_session.go:26` and `:135` — 2
- `/bench/repo/server/auth/token.go:194`
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service_storage.go:209`
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go:154`
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sso_username.go:15`
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_access_tokens.go:84`
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/authz_test.go:65`
- `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go:576`

Production-only (non-`_test.go`) that is 7 call sites.

**Runner-up: `(*filter.Engine).CompileToStatement` — `/bench/repo/internal/filter/engine.go:74` — 38 raw call sites, but only 7 are outside its own package.**

Important caveat on the metric: if you count *raw* call sites anywhere in the repo including a package's own tests, `CompileToStatement` actually leads (38), followed by `filter.NewEngine` at `/bench/repo/internal/filter/engine.go:24` (32). But 31 of `CompileToStatement`'s 38 and 30 of `NewEngine`'s 32 are self-calls from `internal/filter/{engine,functions,time}_test.go`, i.e. not true fan-in. Excluding same-package tests:

| symbol | decl | external call sites | prod-only |
|---|---|---|---|
| `util.GenUUID` | internal/util/util.go:40 | 28 | 7 |
| `(*filter.Engine).CompileToStatement` | internal/filter/engine.go:74 | 7 (6 external + `internal/filter/helpers.go:11`) | 7 |
| `filter.DefaultEngine` | internal/filter/engine.go:111 | 7 | 7 |
| `filter.AppendConditions` | internal/filter/helpers.go:9 | 6 | 6 |
| `util.ConvertStringToInt32` | internal/util/util.go:14 | 5 | 5 |
| `s3.NewClient` | internal/storage/s3/s3.go:25 | 5 | 5 |
| `filter.DefaultAttachmentEngine` | internal/filter/engine.go:119 | 4 | 4 |

Also worth noting: `internal/base/resource_name.go` declares **no functions at all** in this revision — only the `UIDMatcher` regexp var (`/bench/repo/internal/base/resource_name.go:6`), which has 0 references outside its own test. So the `base.ConvertToPascalCase` example from the question does not exist here.

Non-obvious dead/near-dead exports found along the way (0 callers): `util.HasPrefixes` (util.go:23), `util.ValidateEmail` (util.go:33), `util.ReplaceString` (util.go:66), `version.GetMinorVersion` (version.go:23), `webhook.Post` (webhook.go:120), `httpgetter.GetHTMLMeta` (html_meta.go:136) and `httpgetter.GetImage` (image.go:16), `email.NewClient` (client.go:20).

## Q2 — Store entity type referenced from the most non-store packages

**1st: `store.User` — `/bench/repo/store/user.go:29` — 7 distinct packages outside `store/`, 89 references.**

- `server/router/api/v1` (55)
- `server/router/fileserver` (12)
- `server/router/api/v1/test` (7)
- `server/auth` (6)
- `server/notification` (5)
- `server/router/rss` (3)
- `server/router/frontend` (1)

**2nd: `store.Memo` — `/bench/repo/store/memo.go:35` — 6 distinct packages outside `store/`, 59 references.**

- `server/router/api/v1` (33)
- `server/router/api/v1/test` (10)
- `server/notification` (10)
- `server/router/rss` (3)
- `server/router/frontend` (2)
- `server/runner/memopayload` (1)

3rd is `store.Attachment` (`/bench/repo/store/attachment.go:16`) with 4 packages / 43 refs: `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/rss`.

Full ranking by distinct non-store packages: `User` 7, `Memo` 6, `Attachment` 4, `Inbox` 3, `MemoRelation` 3, `MemoShare` 3, `Visibility` 3, `Reaction` 2, `UserIdentity` 2, `UserSetting` 1, `InstanceSetting` 1, `IdentityProvider` 1.

Note the ordering flips if you include `store/`-internal consumers (`store/db/{mysql,postgres,sqlite}` and `store/test`): `User` 11 pkgs vs `Memo` 10 pkgs — `User` still wins, though `Memo` has heavier usage inside `store/test`.

Also: `store.Activity`, `store.Workspace`, and `store.Resource` from the question **do not exist** in this revision. `Resource` was renamed to `Attachment` (`store/attachment.go`), and there is no activity or workspace entity — the closest analogues are `store.InstanceSetting` (`/bench/repo/store/instance_setting.go:14`) and `store.Inbox` (`/bench/repo/store/inbox.go:24`). The `store.Store` handle itself (`/bench/repo/store/store.go:13`) appears in 12 packages, but it is a service/DI object rather than a persistent entity.
